findings.title: localCache is populated before the store write, so the device limit is silently bypassed
findings.body: tagDeviceUI() calls a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{}) before CreateOrUpdateDevice(). When the device limit is reached and CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the cache entry remains, so every subsequent request with the same device id returns nil early (for the 29-minute cache TTL) and the anonymous client authenticates successfully. The limit is therefore enforced only for the first request of each new device and then effectively bypassed, and behaviour differs per Grafana instance (each has its own local cache). The cache entry should only be set after a successful store write.

findings.title: updateDevice reports ErrDeviceLimitReached when MySQL reports 0 changed rows for an existing device
findings.body: updateDevice treats rowsAffected == 0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached. With MySQL, UPDATE reports the number of *changed* rows, so an existing, known device whose client_ip/user_agent/updated_at values are unchanged (e.g. repeated requests within the same second, since MySQL datetime precision is seconds) yields 0 and the user is wrongly rejected as over the device limit even though the device is already tracked. Consider checking for row existence separately or relying on a SELECT before deciding.

findings.title: Count-then-insert is not atomic; the device limit can be exceeded
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts devices and then performs the upsert in two separate sessions. Concurrent requests (same instance or multiple Grafana instances sharing the DB) can all read count < deviceLimit and then each insert a new device, exceeding the configured limit by an arbitrary amount. Also, a COUNT(*) query is now executed on every tagged request, adding DB load on the authentication hot path.

findings.title: Device tagging moved onto the synchronous authentication path
findings.body: TagDevice is now called inline in Authenticate with the request context instead of in a background goroutine. Every anonymous request now blocks on a COUNT query plus an upsert/update against the database before authentication completes, which increases request latency and DB pressure for anonymous-heavy instances. If synchronous behaviour is required for limit enforcement, at least the non-limit path should avoid the extra COUNT.

findings.title: Raw ErrDeviceLimitReached returned from Authenticate yields an opaque 500
findings.body: ErrDeviceLimitReached is created with fmt.Errorf and returned directly from Authenticate. The authn layer has no status mapping for it, so a user hitting the device limit gets a generic internal error instead of a meaningful message/status (e.g. errutil with 429/403 and a user-facing message). This makes the new limit undiagnosable for operators and users.

findings.title: New auth.anonymous device_limit setting is undocumented and missing from defaults.ini
findings.body: cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit reads [auth.anonymous] device_limit, but conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini and the anonymous-auth documentation are not updated in this PR. Users have no discoverable way to learn about or configure the new limit, and the setting won't appear in the shipped config files.

findings.title: Frontend type declares anonymousDeviceLimit as possibly undefined while backend always sends a number
findings.body: The backend DTO field AnonymousDeviceLimit is a non-pointer int64 with json tag "anonymousDeviceLimit" (no omitempty), so the value is always present and is 0 when no limit is configured. Typing it as `number | undefined` in GrafanaConfig (and initialising it to `undefined` in GrafanaBootConfig) means consumers must handle a state that never occurs while the real "no limit" signal (0) is untyped/undocumented. Either make it `number` with a documented 0 meaning, or omit the field server-side when unset.
